When water freezes, the molecules arrange into a hexagonal crystalline lattice stabilized by hydrogen bonds. The hydrogen bonds in ice form a rigid, three-dimensional network that holds molecules farther apart, reducing the overall density of ice. Since ice is less dense than liquid water, it floats.
